minutes.headline: Committee reworked master plan housing and land-use priorities; town-building specifics still deferred
minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee, meeting remotely, walked line-by-line through the consultant team's response to its earlier must-have/nice-to-have list, reworking or reclassifying items on housing (missing-middle housing, inclusionary zoning, affordable housing trust fund), land use (sewer-area density, farmland strategy), economic development, and walkability/complete streets. No formal vote was taken on any master plan recommendation itself; the committee did vote to approve the June 25 minutes with edits and to adjourn. Next steps agreed were to finalize a feedback spreadsheet for other town boards (due back around early-to-mid September) and to hold a further public meeting in October before the plan is finished.

votes.motion: approve the June 25 meeting minutes with two edits: add date/location/time, and distinguish member versus non-member attendees

budget_items.what_was_said: A town official said the short-to-medium-term budget likely has no funds for the town to purchase prime developable land, in response to a must-have item about assessing purchase of the town center.

budget_items.topic: state Affordable Housing Trust Fund allocation
budget_items.what_was_said: The consultant said the state allocates substantial funding annually to municipalities and nonprofits through the trust fund program, which costs the town only staff time to set up.

budget_items.topic: economic development director / small business funding
budget_items.what_was_said: A town official said a back-of-the-napkin calculation by government professionals found an economic development director would not generate enough tax revenue to pay for the position, so the committee dropped funding-based small business support in favor of easier permitting.
The consultant said the state's Complete Streets program can provide construction funding to a town that adopts a Complete Streets policy and prioritization plan.

decisions.decision: Rework the townhouse recommendation into a broader 'missing middle' housing recommendation covering a range of housing types.
Reword the inclusionary zoning must-have to 'study the impacts of inclusionary zoning on development feasibility.'
Upgrade the affordable housing trust fund item to a must-have, since it costs the town little beyond staff time.
Restore the farmland inventory/strategy item as a must-have rather than dropping it.
Confirm 'make the town center more walkable' remains a must-have, as previously voted.
Drop dedicated small-business startup funding; focus instead on easing bylaws/permitting for new businesses.
Combine competing 30 School Street proposals into 'develop options for green space or parking,' with parking prioritized for now.
Keep only a general 'inventory and create a long-term plan for all town land and buildings' item, since specific building reuse proposals have repeatedly failed at town meeting.
Keep sidewalk/bike connectivity items as nice-to-have, flagged with a feasibility/cost caveat rather than removed.
Distribute the committee feedback spreadsheet only to chairs and vice chairs of other boards, not full boards, to avoid open meeting law issues.
Target roughly early-to-mid September for other town boards/committees to return feedback on the draft recommendations.
Briefly present the master plan's current state at the upcoming town meeting without seeking a vote, and hold a fuller public listening session in October.

what_happened.line: No formal vote was taken on the master plan itself; the committee voted to approve the June 25 minutes with edits, then voted to adjourn.
A townhouse-specific housing proposal was reworked into a broader 'missing middle' housing recommendation.
An affordable housing trust fund item was upgraded to a must-have, since setting it up costs the town mainly staff time.
Dedicated small-business startup funding and an economic development director position were dropped in favor of easing permitting for new businesses.
The committee agreed to send other boards a feedback spreadsheet, limited to chairs and vice chairs, and to hold a further public meeting before finishing the plan.

why_it_matters: These reworked items on housing types, inclusionary zoning and an affordable housing trust fund will feed into zoning bylaw changes residents eventually vote on at town meeting.
Dropping a funded economic-development position in favor of permitting changes affects how the town supports small businesses without adding a new budget line.
The plan is not finished: other town boards and the public still get a formal round of review before any recommendation reaches a town meeting warrant.

reconciliation.summary: The records agree on topic and broad outcomes for the draft recommendations (affordable housing trust to must-have, farmland strategy to must-have, town center walkability must-have), but the official minutes are a bullet outline with no vote record other than adjournment, and the two differ on who attended, on the 30 School Street disposition, and on several decisions only one side records. The one thing to know: the 30 School Street outcome (parking prioritized in ours, "Nice to Have" green space in the official) and the unrecorded committee chair identity and attendee roster should be checked against the recording.
